messages.subject: Scan Pack is killing deals - I need us to look at this
messages.body:
Hola equipo,

Straight talk: Scan Pack has become the thing every deal stumbles on 🚨 Prospects love the pitch until the pricing conversation turns to "how many scans will you do per month?" - nobody knows the answer, so everyone assumes the worst, and my average sales cycle for scan-using accounts has gone from three weeks to nearly seven. Two prospects this week asked me to "come back when the pricing is simpler". That is the polite version.

Our competitors sell one number. We are selling a base plan plus a variable component that requires the customer to forecast their own scanner behaviour. For the mid-market, that friction alone loses deals. Can we please revisit this?

Saludos,
Tomás

messages.subject: RE: Scan Pack is killing deals - I need us to look at this
messages.body:
Hi team 😊

Tomás is not exaggerating, I am afraid. Support has logged 23 Scan Pack tickets this month alone, and they are almost all confusion rather than faults: customers cannot tell whether a scan counts before or after the free allowance, three of our heavy users have asked for a PDF of "what exactly is a scan", and we had one genuinely upset customer (Biesbosch Transport again, poor Hans) whose first metered invoice was 40% higher than his base plan. He paid it, but he has asked us twice since to confirm it will not happen again.

Every ticket takes longer than a normal ticket because we are explaining pricing maths, not fixing software. I would rather my team spent that time on actual problems.

Warm regards,
Aisha

Aisha Bello
Head of Customer Success, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: Scan Pack is killing deals - I need us to look at this
messages.body:
Adding the engineering angle, my take:

- The metered line item is the single most complicated thing in the new Ledgerly billing setup. Every settlement so far has had an edge case: scans recorded during the free-allowance boundary, mid-cycle allowance changes, backdated scan corrections.
- Cutover is 6 July. Carrying a metered component through our first live Ledgerly cycle is exactly the kind of complexity I said I did not want in that window.
- If we keep Scan Pack, I need one engineer on billing reconciliation for two extra weeks. If we drop it and fold a flat allowance into the plan price, the billing change is trivial and the cutover gets simpler.

Cheers, Dev

messages.subject: RE: Scan Pack is killing deals - I need us to look at this
messages.body:
Quick recap, and I will be honest that I am reluctant here:

1. Scan Pack exists because a handful of accounts genuinely cost us 3-4x the median to serve, and that cost has not gone away. 2. But the feedback is consistent and loud: sales friction (Tomás), 23 confusion tickets (Aisha), and real billing risk in the cutover window (Dev). 3. Middle option would be keeping Scan Pack only for the top few heavy accounts - but that is bespoke pricing, which I dislike even more. 4. My suggestion: drop Scan Pack and include 500 scans/month in the Pro plan. It keeps a signal in the pricing for scan-heavy buyers, gets them onto a higher plan tier instead of a metered bill, and 500 covers what a normal courier actually does. We give up some margin on the heaviest users, but they were costing us goodwill we cannot afford either.

Thanks!
Priya

messages.subject: RE: Scan Pack is killing deals - I need us to look at this
messages.body:
Dear Marta,

I will not block this: I accept that a pricing construct which confuses customers, slows sales and complicates a cutover is costing us more than the margin it protects. I would gently note for the record that the scan-heavy cohort was roughly €3k/month of usage revenue at risk of reduction, and I will model the net effect of moving those accounts to Pro at the new allowance once Priya has final numbers. One request: whatever we announce to customers with existing Scan Pack arrangements, let us make the transition seamless for their next invoice, not their next quarter.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.body: Thank you!! "One plan, 500 scans included" is a pitch I can make on the phone in one sentence ✅🚀 I'll rewrite the two stuck proposals today.
